en: The Banaue Rice Terraces use the simple machine of an inclined plane to help farmers grow crops on steep mountain slopes.
A carabao’s wide, splayed hooves increase friction to prevent slipping while plowing muddy rice fields in the Philippines.
Gravity pulls the water of Maria Cristina Falls downward, converting potential energy into kinetic energy to generate electricity.
Japan’s SCMaglev train uses powerful superconducting magnets to levitate above the tracks, eliminating friction for ultra-fast travel.
Alessandro Volta invented the voltaic pile in 1800, creating the world’s first true battery to produce steady electrical current.
Fireflies along Bohol’s Loboc River produce bioluminescent light through a chemical reaction in their abdomens to attract mates.
Sound waves reflect off the curved dome of St. Paul’s Cathedral in London, creating a famous echoing whispering gallery.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay harnesses underground heat from magma to boil water and spin turbines.
A leaping Tamaraw in Mounts Iglit-Baco National Park demonstrates kinetic energy as its heavy body moves through the air.
Ferdinand Magellan’s ship Victoria used a block and tackle pulley system to multiply force when raising heavy sails.
The rubber treads on MRT-3 train wheels increase friction against the rails to prevent dangerous slipping during braking.
The Navotas Solar Plant uses photovoltaic cells to transform radiant light energy from the sun into usable electrical energy.
